subject: Ahmad et al. (1998)
object: Ahmad et al. (1998) described a large, inbred, 8-generation kindred from a remote area of Pakistan with a distinct form of spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia. They evaluated 16 affected individuals (11 males and 5 females). Clinical findings included short stature evident at birth, short bowed lower limbs, mild brachydactyly, kyphoscoliosis, an abnormal gait, enlarged knee joints, precocious osteoarthropathy, and normal intelligence.

subject: Ahmad et al. (1998)
object: Ahmad et al. (1998) reported that radiographs showed delayed epiphyseal ossification at the hips and knees, platyspondyly with irregular end plates and narrowed joint spaces, diffuse early osteoarthritic changes mainly in the spine and hands, and mild brachydactyly. Mild metaphyseal abnormalities were seen mostly at the hips and knees.

subject: Ahmad et al. (1998)
object: Ahmad et al. (1998) concluded that pedigree analysis strongly suggested autosomal recessive inheritance. Consanguineous loops could explain all affected individuals being homozygous for the abnormal allele.

subject: Ahmad et al. (1998)
object: Ahmad et al. (1998) concluded that this phenotype is distinct from other autosomal recessive forms of SEMD. They based this on the mild metaphyseal involvement, the type of brachydactyly, and the absence of loose joints or other clinical findings.

subject: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998)
object: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) studied a large inbred Pakistani family with a distinct form of recessively inherited spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (SEMD), a dwarfing condition.

subject: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998)
object: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) found that SEMD in a large inbred Pakistani family was inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.

subject: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998)
object: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) mapped the gene associated with SEMD in a large inbred Pakistani family to chromosome 10q23-24, a region syntenic with the locus for the brachymorphic mutation on mouse chromosome 19.

subject: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998)
object: In affected members of a large inbred Pakistani family with SEMD, Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) identified a nonsense mutation in the ATPSK2 gene, which encodes a novel ATP sulfurylase/APS kinase that catalyzes the activation of inorganic sulfate to PAPS.

subject: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998)
object: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) identified a missense mutation in the region of Atpsk2 encoding the APS kinase activity in the brachymorphic mouse, the orthologous locus on mouse chromosome 19.

subject: PAPSS2 missense mutation in the region of Atpsk2 encoding the APS kinase activity
Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998)
object: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) concluded that the cartilage specificity of the human and mouse phenotypes provided evidence of the critical role of sulfate activation to PAPS, the universal donor for protein sulfation, in maturation of cartilage extracellular matrix molecules and skeletogenesis.

subject: Noordam et al. (2009)
object: Noordam et al. (2009) described a girl with premature pubarche, hyperandrogenic anovulation, very low DHEAS levels, and increased androgen levels.

subject: Noordam et al. (2009)
object: In a girl with premature pubarche and androgen excess, Noordam et al. (2009) identified compound heterozygous mutations in the PAPSS2 gene. In vitro coincubation of human SULT2A1 with wild-type or mutant PAPSS2 proteins confirmed that the mutations were inactivating.

subject: Noordam et al. (2009)
object: Noordam et al. (2009) noted that SULT2A1 converts DHEA to its inactive sulfate ester DHEAS, preventing conversion of DHEA to active androgens, and requires PAPS for catalytic activity. They concluded that PAPSS2 deficiency is a monogenic adrenocortical cause of androgen excess.

subject: Miyake et al. (2012)
object: Miyake et al. (2012) described 6 patients with autosomal recessive brachyolmia: 3 affected members of a Turkish family, 2 Japanese patients, and 1 Korean patient. The patients had short-trunk short stature that became conspicuous during childhood, with normal intelligence and facies. Radiographic features included rectangular vertebral bodies with irregular endplates and narrow intervertebral discs, precocious calcification of rib cartilages, short femoral neck, and mildly shortened metacarpals; spinal changes were very similar among the 6 patients, whereas epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes of the tubular bones were variable.

subject: Miyake et al. (2012)
object: In 3 affected members of a Turkish family with autosomal recessive brachyolmia, Miyake et al. (2012) used exon capture followed by next-generation sequencing and identified a homozygous loss-of-function mutation in the PAPSS2 gene, c.337_338insG (p.A113GfsX18).

subject: Miyake et al. (2012)
object: Miyake et al. (2012) identified homozygosity for a PAPSS2 splice mutation, IVS3+2delT, in 1 of 3 additional patients (2 Japanese and 1 Korean) with a similar brachyolmia phenotype.

subject: Miyake et al. (2012)
object: Miyake et al. (2012) identified compound heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in PAPSS2, c.616-634del19 (p.V206SfsX9) and c.1309-1310delAG (p.R437GfsX19), in a patient with brachyolmia (one of 2 Japanese and 1 Korean patients studied).

subject: Miyake et al. (2012)
object: Miyake et al. (2012) identified compound heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in PAPSS2, c.480_481insCGTA (p.K161RfsX6) and c.661delA (p.I221SfsX40), in a patient with brachyolmia (one of 2 Japanese and 1 Korean patients studied).

subject: Miyake et al. (2012)
object: Miyake et al. (2012) concluded that PAPSS2 mutations produce a skeletal dysplasia family with a gradation of phenotypes ranging from brachyolmia to spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia.

subject: Miyake et al. (2012)
object: Miyake et al. (2012) noted that brachyolmia is clinically and genetically heterogeneous, with TRPV4 mutations causing an autosomal dominant form, and identified PAPSS2 as a disease gene for an autosomal recessive form.
